name: Goidel

attributes.attribute: literary ancestor of the Goidelic Celts of Ireland, Scotland, and the Isle of Man
grandson of an Egyptian Pharaoh and healed by Moses in a Christianized text
given a Greek pedigree by Edmund Spenser as a son of Cecrops of Argos
created the Irish language by joining words from 72 languages
ancestor who spoke Scots Gaelic at the Tower of Babel

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Goidel, also called Gadelus or Gaedhal, is an Irish hero. Scholars believe he is a literary invention, not a real divinity. He is named the ancestor of the Goidelic Celts of Ireland, Scotland, and the Isle of Man. One Christianized account says Moses healed him in boyhood and names an Egyptian Pharaoh his grandfather. Edmund Spenser gave him a Greek pedigree as a son of Cecrops of Argos. Goidel wed a princess of Egypt and took her to Spain. He may equal Míl of the Milesians. His ancestor Rifath Scot spoke Scots Gaelic at the Tower of Babel. Goidel built the Irish language by joining words from the 72 languages he knew.

okr.objective: Explain Goidel as the invented ancestor of the Goidelic Celts and creator of Irish.
key_results: Goidel is a literary invention named as ancestor of the Goidelic Celts.
A Christianized text makes him a grandson of an Egyptian Pharaoh healed by Moses.
Spenser gave him a Greek pedigree through Cecrops of Argos.
He joined words of 72 languages to make Irish.
